ANA@PHI.text: A near coin flip between the model's 23rd and 24th rated teams. Philadelphia (3-6-3) has won three straight after an 0-6-3 start, while Anaheim (4-6-0) has lost five in a row. The Flyers are still without Konecny, Tippett, York and Grebenkin, though Ristolainen no longer appears on ESPN's injury list and could return. Anaheim is missing Terry and Poehling and put Mintyukov on IR Friday. Woll is confirmed for Philadelphia; Dostal is expected for Anaheim.

LAK@NJD.text: New Jersey traded for Connor Hellebuyck on Friday, but he will not play, so Jake Allen is the projected starter. The Devils (6-4-0) are 4-1 in their last five and rate 6th in the model. Los Angeles (2-4-2) has won two straight but is without Kevin Fiala (leg surgery) and Alex Turcotte, and Quinton Byfield is questionable. Lowest projected total on the slate at 5.81.

SJS@BOS.text: The slate's biggest favorite. Boston (8-2-1) routed Nashville 6-0 Thursday and David Pastrnak has 16 points in 11 games; projected starter Jeremy Swayman carries one of the best goalie numbers on the board. San Jose has won two straight behind Macklin Celebrini (14 points in 9 games), but Askarov needed 41 saves while the Sharks were outshot 43-28, and the model rates them 29th. Winger Igor Chernyshov is expected to miss time after taking a shot off the arm.

NYR@OTT.text: Ottawa confirmed Jonas Johansson in net (TSN 1200), not Samuel Ersson. With Ullmark on IR, that is a modest upgrade over Ersson's weak early numbers and lifts Ottawa from 49% to 52%. The Rangers are thin in net, with Shesterkin out for the season and Korpisalo hurt, so Dylan Garand is projected. New York (7-4-1) has lost four straight on the road; Ottawa is also missing Chabot and Eklund.

NSH@PIT.text: One of the highest projected totals on the slate (6.68). Nashville (3-3-3) is coming off a 6-0 loss in Boston and has struggled to finish at 5-on-5; Juuse Saros rested Thursday and is now projected by both the model and Daily Faceoff. Pittsburgh snapped a four-game skid with a 4-0 win over Florida behind an Arturs Silovs shutout, and Silovs was first off the ice at Saturday's morning skate. Evgeni Malkin (illness) and Egor Chinakhov are now listed out, along with Rust and Kindel on IR; the model rates Malkin's even-strength impact near average this season and Chinakhov's below average, so the line barely moves.

BUF@WSH.text: Biggest goalie swing of the morning: Charlie Lindgren is confirmed for Washington with Logan Thompson day to day, which drops the Capitals from 58% to a coin flip (50%) and pushes the projected total to 6.92, the highest on the slate. Alex Tuch faces Buffalo for the first time since his sign-and-trade and has 7 points in 9 games. The Capitals are also without Desharnais (appendectomy); Buffalo (4-4-2) has ruled out Jiri Kulich, a small hit to its even-strength play.

VGK@CBJ.text: Columbus is likely starting Cam Talbot, who took the starter's crease at morning skate, instead of Jet Greaves; that moves Vegas from 53% to 58%. The model rates Vegas 3rd and Columbus (3-5-0) 20th. Vegas's starter is still unconfirmed: the model projects Adin Hill, whose early numbers are weak, while Daily Faceoff lists Carter Hart, which would widen Vegas's edge. Mitch Marner is now listed out, a small dent in Vegas's edge (58% to 57.8%).

CAR@STL.text: Carolina (8-2-2) leads the NHL in points and is the model's top team by expected-goal differential, even with Taylor Hall, Jordan Staal and Alexander Nikishin on IR. St. Louis (5-4-1) has won two straight but carries a long injury list, including Krug, Dube, Toropchenko, Tucker and Mailloux. Kochetkov and Hofer are projected.

TOR@EDM.text: Edmonton (8-1-1) is first in the Pacific and Connor McDavid has 31 points in 10 games, but the goaltending is unsettled: Devon Levi, who started 7 of 10, will miss the game and Tristan Jarry is confirmed to start. Jarry's numbers are below expected so far, and Mattias Ekholm, one of the league's most valuable defensemen by on-ice impact, is out 1 to 2 weeks with a head injury; Edmonton recalled Matt Tomkins as the backup. Together they trim Edmonton from 60.8% to 56.8%. Toronto (6-4-2) is without John Tavares (lower body, not traveling on the four-game trip), Chris Tanev and Max Domi. Toronto's starter is unconfirmed: the model uses Bobrovsky, while Daily Faceoff now projects Anthony Stolarz.

TBL@UTA.text: Tampa Bay is on a back-to-back after a 6-3 loss in Colorado Friday, which the model treats as a meaningful drag. Vasilevskiy started Friday, so the model rotates to Dennis Hildeby; Daily Faceoff still lists Vasilevskiy, and his start would make this closer to even. Both teams rate in the model's top 8. Utah (7-4-0) lists John Marino as day to day.

DET@CGY.text: Detroit is favored, but its goaltending is the biggest open question on the slate: John Gibson left Thursday's game in Vancouver with an upper-body injury and Daniil Tarasov is listed day to day. Tarasov is expected to start per this morning's previews, and the model now uses him; his numbers are close to Gibson's, so Detroit's edge barely changes. Calgary (3-6-0) has won two straight but rates 30th; the model projects Dustin Wolf, while Daily Faceoff lists Devin Cooley, who started the last two. Backlund is day to day and Huberdeau is on IR.

MIN@SEA.text: The model's clearest road favorite. Seattle is 7-3-1, but its underlying numbers rate 27th, while Minnesota rates 4th. The Wild are banged up, with Gustavsson, both Folignos and Brock Faber out, but projected starter Jesper Wallstedt has been strong. Seattle is without Ryan Lindgren and has now ruled out Jared McCann, which trims the Kraken from 40% to 39%.
